chapter_title: I’m Up and Down, and Round and Round

zero_omission_notes.summary: This chapter provides a rigorous axiomatic study of circular geometry. Topics include locus definition of circle, radius, chord, diameter, arc, sector, segment, circumcircle construction around 3 non-collinear points (circumcentre), equal chord theorems, perpendicular bisector of chord passing through centre, inscribed angle theorem, angle subtended by arc at centre vs circumference, angle in a semicircle, concyclicity, and cyclic quadrilaterals.

detailed_sections.full_notes: A circle is the set of all points in a plane equidistant from a fixed centre point O. The perpendicular from centre O to a chord bisects the chord. Equal chords are equidistant from the centre.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Uniqueness of Circumcircle
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: There is one and only one circle passing through three given non-collinear points.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 5.2 Arc Subtended Angles & Inscribed Angle Theorem
detailed_sections.full_notes: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle: angle AOB = 2 * angle ACB.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Angles in Segments
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: 1. Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal. 2. Angle subtended in a semicircle is a right angle (90 degrees).

detailed_sections.full_notes: A quadrilateral is cyclic if all four vertices lie on a circle. The sum of either pair of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180 degrees (supplementary).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Concyclicity Condition
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: If the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is 180 degrees, the quadrilateral is cyclic.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: Finding Centre of a Given Circle / Circular Arc
procedure_or_steps: Trace boundary of coin on paper to get circle.
Draw two non-parallel chords AB and CD on the circle.
Construct perpendicular bisector of chord AB using compass.
Construct perpendicular bisector of chord CD.
Mark point of intersection of perpendicular bisectors as centre O.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: Perpendicular bisectors of any two chords meet at a single point.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: The perpendicular bisector of every chord passes through the centre.

diagrams_figures_and_maps.drawing_or_reading_instructions: Draw circle with centre O. Mark arc AB at bottom. Connect A and B to O and to C on top circumference.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Point of intersection of perpendicular bisectors of sides of a triangle, serving as center of circumcircle.
A quadrilateral whose four vertices lie on the circumference of a single circle.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: In cyclic ABCD, angle A + angle C = 180 degrees.

textbook_exercises.question: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, if angle A = 75 degrees and angle B = 100 degrees, find angles C and D.
textbook_exercises.answer: angle A + angle C = 180 => angle C = 105 degrees. angle B + angle D = 180 => angle D = 80 degrees.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: What is the measure of an angle subtended in a semicircle?
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: A semicircle arc subtends 180 degrees at centre, so inscribed angle is 180/2 = 90 degrees.

short_answer_questions.question: A chord of length 16 cm is at a distance of 6 cm from centre of circle. Find radius.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: An arc subtends 140 degrees at centre. Calculate angle subtended by it on major arc.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Prove that the sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180 degrees.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer:
1. Let ABCD be cyclic quadrilateral with centre O.
2. Join OA and OC.
3. Reflex angle AOC = 2 * angle ADC (Inscribed Angle Theorem).
4. Acute angle AOC = 2 * angle ABC.
5. Reflex angle AOC + Acute angle AOC = 360 degrees.
6. 2 * angle ADC + 2 * angle ABC = 360 => angle ADC + angle ABC = 180 degrees.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Three satellite tracking stations A, B, C are located on a circular radar display boundary around central server O.

qa.question: If station angle ABC is measured as 50 degrees, what is angle AOC on server monitor?
qa.answer: Central angle AOC = 2 * angle ABC = 2 * 50 = 100 degrees.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Assuming any quadrilateral drawn inside a circle is cyclic.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: A quadrilateral is cyclic ONLY if all four vertices lie strictly on the circle boundary.
